newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 0.5 pct w/e May 24 -Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 0.5 pct w/e May 24 -Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the period ending May 24 versus April's final estimate, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 6.0 percent compared to the same period a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 5.3 percent in the week ended May 24 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Retailers pointed their fingers at cooler weather, which lingered in the Midwest and Northeast, for the softness in sales this week, a Redbook Research report said.
Discount stores and, to a lesser extent, national department stores, have been particularly affected, said Howard Eilenberg, a research analyst at Redbook Research.
"The (discount) customers pay greater heed to immediate needs and immediate satisfaction," Eilenberg said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
However, seasonal merchandise is reported to be selling in in the warmer regions, like California and Florida, suggesting a timing effect will reverse, Eilenberg said.
"Where the weather is warm, the goods are selling," he said, adding that "I would not press the panic button."
The current sales numbers for the week excluded most of the Memorial Day weekend, but retailers said holiday sales appeared to be very robust.
But Eilenberg said sales for the month will probably come inunder plan.
